column1: prompt
A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 die. How many sheep are left? Explain your reasoning step by step.

A train leaves Chicago at 8am traveling at 60mph toward New York. Another leaves New York at 10am at 80mph toward Chicago. The distance between cities is 790 miles. At what time do they meet? Show all work.

You have three boxes: one contains only apples, one only oranges, and one a mix. All three are mislabeled. You can draw one fruit from one box. How do you determine the contents of all three boxes? Walk through your logic.

A company introduces a free lunch program. Employee satisfaction scores rise by 20%. A manager concludes that free lunch causes satisfaction. Identify at least three alternative explanations and explain how you'd test the causal claim.

You're choosing between two job offers: Offer A pays $95K with a 2-hour commute and great work-life balance. Offer B pays $115K with a 30-minute commute but a high-stress culture. Walk through a structured decision-making process. What additional information would you need?
Five friends sit in a row. Alice is not next to Bob. Carol is to the left of David. Bob is to the right of Eve. Eve is not at either end. List all valid seating arrangements.
How many piano tuners are in Chicago? Walk through a Fermi estimation step by step.
A bag has 3 red and 5 blue marbles. You draw two marbles without replacement. What is the probability that both are blue? Show all steps.

A study finds that countries with higher chocolate consumption have more Nobel Prize winners per capita. Is this evidence that chocolate makes people smarter? What confounders explain this? How would you design a study to test causality?

You're a product manager and must cut two features from a release due to an engineering shortfall. Your team has built features A (high impact, 80% complete), B (medium impact, 95% complete), C (low impact, 30% complete), and D (high impact, 50% complete). Walk through your decision framework.
In a village, every barber shaves exactly those people who do not shave themselves. Does the barber shave himself? Explain the paradox fully.
You invest $10,000 at 7% annual compound interest. How much will it be worth after 20 years? After how many years will it double? Show your calculations.
How many golf balls fit in a school bus? Show your Fermi approach with labeled assumptions.
Ice cream sales and drowning rates are correlated. Explain why this is not causation. What is the correct causal model? How would you visualize it using a causal diagram?

You have $500 to spend on marketing for a local restaurant. Your options are: Google Ads (measurable, delayed), flyers (cheap, low targeting), Instagram ads (visual, fast feedback), or partnering with a food blogger (uncertain, high potential). How do you allocate the budget and why?

Four cards are on a table, each with a letter on one side and a number on the other. You see: A, K, 4, 7. Which cards must you flip to test the rule 'If a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other'?
What is the probability that in a group of 23 randomly chosen people, at least two share a birthday? Explain the birthday problem intuitively and mathematically.
How much data (in GB) does a typical Netflix user stream per month? Walk through your assumptions.

A school introduces a new reading program and test scores rise. The principal says the program caused the improvement. What three alternative hypotheses would a methodologically rigorous evaluator consider first?

Your startup has runway for 6 months. You can: (a) raise a bridge round now at unfavorable terms, (b) cut 30% of staff to extend runway to 12 months, or (c) aggressively close two large enterprise deals. What is your decision framework and which factors are most important?
You have a 3-gallon jug and a 5-gallon jug. How do you measure exactly 4 gallons of water? Walk through each step.
A rectangle's length is twice its width. Its perimeter is 48cm. What are its dimensions and area? Show all steps.
Sales of sunscreen and ice cream both spike in summer. Does sunscreen cause ice cream sales? Identify the common cause and draw the causal structure.
How many text messages are sent per day in India? Walk through a Fermi estimation with labeled assumptions.
You must choose between renting an apartment (₹25,000/month, flexible) or buying one (₹60L purchase price, 8.5% loan for 20 years). You plan to stay 5 years. Walk through the financial reasoning.
A light switch controls one of three lights in another room. You can flip switches as many times as you want before entering the room (once). How do you identify which switch controls which light?
A jar contains 4 red, 3 blue, and 5 green marbles. You draw 3 without replacement. What is the probability that you get exactly one of each color? Show full working.
A new helmet law is passed and bicycle accident deaths fall 20%. A politician says helmets saved lives. What alternative explanations exist? How would you test causality?
Prove that the sum of the first N odd numbers equals N². Show the proof by induction.

You have three freelance project offers: Project A pays ₹80K for 2 weeks of work with a reliable client. Project B pays ₹150K for 6 weeks with a new client and unclear scope. Project C pays ₹50K for 1 week during a week you already have a vacation planned. How do you decide?
There are 100 prisoners and 100 boxes each containing a number 1–100. Each prisoner can open 50 boxes. If all find their number, all go free. What strategy gives the best chance of success and why?
How many hours of YouTube video are watched globally per day? Walk through your assumptions.
A social media platform notices users who follow more than 500 accounts have lower engagement rates. Should it cap follows? Identify the causal story and what you'd need to verify.
Two workers can complete a job in 6 hours working together. Worker A alone takes 10 hours. How long does Worker B take alone? Show the work-rate reasoning.
Your laptop is 4 years old and just got a cracked screen (₹12,000 repair). A new laptop costs ₹65,000. Walk through the decision using expected value and opportunity cost reasoning.
You have 12 balls, one of which is slightly heavier or lighter. Using a balance scale in exactly 3 weighings, identify the odd ball and whether it is heavier or lighter. Walk through the strategy.
How many WhatsApp messages are sent in India per day? Walk through your Fermi estimate with explicit assumptions.
A company's revenue grows at 8% per year. A competitor's grows at 12% per year. The competitor currently has half your revenue. In how many years will they overtake you? Show all algebra.
You are offered two payment options for freelance work: ₹50,000 upfront or ₹8,000/month for 8 months. Assuming a 10% annual discount rate, which is worth more in present value terms? Show your work.

A gym observes that members who use personal trainers have better fitness outcomes. Should it force all members to use trainers? Identify selection bias and explain why this would not replicate the observed effect.
You roll two fair six-sided dice. What is the probability that their sum is at least 9? List all favorable outcomes and show the calculation.
Three friends — Aarav, Bina, and Chetan — each order a different dish: biryani, dosa, and paneer. Aarav does not like rice. Bina is vegetarian. Chetan did not order dosa. Who ordered what?
How many software engineers are currently employed in Bengaluru? Walk through your estimate using population, employment rate, and tech sector share.
If you fold a piece of paper in half 42 times (hypothetically), how thick would it be? Show the calculation and compare to the distance from Earth to the Moon.
100 people stand in a circle. Every second person is eliminated until one remains. Which position should you stand in to be the last survivor? Derive the formula.
A hospital implements a new hand-washing protocol and infection rates drop. But they also hired more staff that month. How do you isolate the protocol effect? Describe the study design you'd need.
How many books are published per year globally? Walk through a Fermi estimate covering traditional, self-published, and digital-only titles.
A train leaves City A at 9am going 60mph. Another train leaves City B (200 miles away) at 10am going 80mph toward City A. At what time do they meet? Show your work step by step.

You have 12 balls, one of which is slightly heavier or lighter than the others. You have a balance scale and 3 weighings. Describe the strategy to find the odd ball and determine if it's heavier or lighter.
Three people each make one true and one false statement. Given their statements, determine who is the liar, who always tells the truth, and who alternates.
A company's revenue grew 15% in year 1, declined 10% in year 2, and grew 20% in year 3. What was the net percentage change over 3 years? Why is this different from simply adding the percentages?
If you invest $10,000 at 7% annual compound interest, how long will it take to double? Use the rule of 72 and then verify with the exact formula. Explain when each is appropriate.

You have two job offers: Job A pays $120k with no equity, great work-life balance, and 10% annual raise. Job B pays $90k with 0.5% equity in a Series A startup, 60-hour weeks, and high risk of failure. Walk through a structured framework for deciding between them.

A software team is deciding whether to fix technical debt now (costing 3 sprints) or ship a new feature first (risking 6–9 sprints of slowdown later). Analyze the tradeoffs using expected value reasoning.

User retention for a mobile app dropped 15% the week after a major UI redesign. List all plausible alternative explanations beyond 'the redesign caused it' and explain what data you'd need to rule each out.
A study found that cities with more ice cream shops have higher murder rates. Explain why this is not a causal relationship and identify the confounding variable.
Estimate how many piano tuners are in Chicago. Show your Fermi estimation approach step by step, including all assumptions and how you'd check your answer.
How many golf balls fit in a school bus? Explain your geometry assumptions and estimation strategy.
A diagnostic test for a disease is 99% accurate. The disease affects 0.1% of the population. If you test positive, what is the actual probability you have the disease? Show using Bayes' theorem.
You flip a fair coin 10 times and get 8 heads. Is the coin likely biased? Calculate the probability of getting 8 or more heads with a fair coin and explain what this means for your conclusion.
